[Pedagogy review · High priority · missing-prerequisite · pf-54d8e7a509]
Simplifying even roots of algebraic powers requires an absolute-value distinction that the preceding teaching never explains.
Before p8-q13-i, add: 'A square root gives the non-negative root. If y = −3, √(y²) = √9 = 3, not −3. Therefore √(y²) = |y|, where |y| is the distance of y from zero. If y ≥ 0, this equals y.' Qualify the p14 key idea: 'When simplifying even roots, retain the non-negative result.'
Also affects: p14-key-ideas-block, p16-q4-g, p18-q18-i

[Pedagogy review · High priority · missing-prerequisite · pf-25b1038867]
The final equation requires recognising and solving a quadratic in an exponential expression, a variant not modelled earlier.
Before p33-q9-c, model: 'Solve 9^x−2 × 3^x−3 = 0. Since 9^x = (3^x)², let t = 3^x. Then t²−2t−3 = (t−3)(t+1) = 0, so t = 3 or −1. Since 3^x > 0, reject −1. Thus 3^x = 3 and x = 1.'
